account.en: to form a part of a total (account for)
account.ex: Exports account for most of the country's income.

affect.ex: The strike will affect thousands of families.

affluent.ex: They live in an affluent part of the city.

example.en: Affluent suburbs often have better schools.
example.zh: 富裕的郊區通常有較好的學校。

note.usage: 比 rich 正式，常修飾 families / areas / society；less affluent 是委婉說「較窮」。

noteEn.usage: More formal than 'rich'; 'less affluent' is a polite way to say poorer.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los barrios acomodados suelen tener mejores colegios.
noteEs.usage: Más formal que 'rich'; 'less affluent' es una forma educada de decir 'más pobre'.

noteHi.exampleTr: समृद्ध उपनगरों में अक्सर बेहतर स्कूल होते हैं।
noteHi.usage: rich से अधिक औपचारिक; less affluent = कम धनी (विनम्र तरीका)।

noteJa.exampleTr: 裕福な郊外には良い学校が多い。
noteJa.usage: rich より改まった語。less affluent は「比較的貧しい」の婉曲表現。

noteKo.exampleTr: 부유한 교외 지역에는 대개 더 좋은 학교가 있다.
noteKo.usage: rich보다 격식; less affluent는 '덜 부유한'의 완곡 표현.

aggregate.ex: Aggregate sales rose by ten per cent last year.

ago.ex: I moved here ten years ago.

almost.ex: It is almost time for dinner.

alternative.ex: We need an alternative route to work.

analysis.ex: Her analysis of the data was very clear.

annual.ex: The school holds an annual sports day.

apply.en: to affect or be used for
apply.ex: The new rule applies to all workers.

approaches.ex: We tried two approaches to the problem.

approximately.ex: The film lasts approximately two hours.

argue.en: to give reasons for an opinion
argue.ex: Critics argue that the plan is too expensive.

asset.ex: Their house is their biggest asset.

assets.ex: The company sold some of its assets.

at.en: in or near a place or time

authors.en: people who wrote a report or book
authors.ex: The authors thanked everyone who helped.

base.en: the things a tax is charged on
base.ex: A wider tax base can lower tax rates.

based.ex: It is a broadly based reform plan.

be.en: to have a quality or state

before.ex: I had seen him two days before.

bigger.ex: It was a big decision for the family.

breadth.en: how wide or wide-ranging something is
breadth.ex: The breadth of her knowledge surprised us.

broadly.ex: The tax is broadly based on income.

business.en: the work of buying, selling or producing
business.ex: She runs a small business in Galway.

businesses.ex: She runs a small business in Galway.

carve-outs.ex: The law has carve-outs for small firms.

cash.en: money you can spend right now
cash.ex: I don't have enough cash for the taxi.

caught.en: included and affected by a rule
caught.ex: Many families were caught by the new tax.

cent.ex: Prices rose by five per cent.

choices.ex: We have two choices for dinner.

close.ex: Close to a thousand people came to the concert.

commands.ex: The party commands a large majority.

commissioned.en: asked someone to do a piece of work
commissioned.ex: The city commissioned a new statue.

compared.en: looked at two things to see differences
compared.ex: She compared the prices in two shops.

conclude.en: decide something is true after studying
conclude.ex: We conclude that the plan works.

concludes.en: decides after thinking about the facts
concludes.ex: The report concludes that prices will rise.

consequently.ex: He missed the bus and consequently was late.

constitute.ex: Women constitute half of the workforce.

example.en: Raising the retirement age is highly contentious.
example.zh: 提高退休年齡極具爭議。

note.meaning: 有爭議的；容易引起爭論的。
note.usage: 常修飾 issue / topic / decision；比 controversial 稍正式。

noteEn.meaning: Likely to cause disagreement and argument.
noteEn.usage: Used with 'issue', 'topic', 'decision'; a bit more formal than 'controversial'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Subir la edad de jubilación es muy polémico.
noteEs.usage: Acompaña a 'issue', 'topic', 'decision'; algo más formal que 'controversial'.

noteHi.exampleTr: सेवानिवृत्ति की उम्र बढ़ाना बहुत विवादास्पद है।
noteHi.meaning: जिस पर लोग असहमत हों और बहस हो।
noteHi.usage: issue/topic/decision के साथ; controversial से थोड़ा औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 定年の引き上げは非常に論争を呼ぶ。
noteJa.meaning: 意見が分かれ、議論を呼びやすいこと。
noteJa.usage: issue / topic / decision などを修飾。controversial よりやや硬い。

noteKo.usage: issue/topic/decision 등을 수식; controversial보다 약간 격식.

continue.ex: The rain will continue all day.

contrast.ex: By contrast, the north was dry and cold.

conversely.ex: Some like hot weather; conversely, others prefer cold.

example.en: Cheap loans boost spending; conversely, high rates slow it.
example.zh: 低息貸款刺激消費；相反地，高利率會抑制消費。

note.usage: 常置句首加逗號，用來引出與前句相反的情況。

noteEn.usage: Often starts a sentence with a comma to give the opposite case.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los préstamos baratos impulsan el gasto; por el contrario, los tipos altos lo frenan.
noteEs.meaning: De forma opuesta; por el contrario.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir al inicio con coma para presentar la situación opuesta.

noteHi.exampleTr: सस्ते ऋण खर्च बढ़ाते हैं; इसके विपरीत, ऊँची दरें उसे धीमा करती हैं।
noteHi.usage: प्रायः वाक्य के आरंभ में अल्पविराम के साथ, उल्टी स्थिति बताने के लिए।

noteJa.exampleTr: 低金利の融資は消費を促し、逆に高金利は消費を抑える。
noteJa.usage: 文頭でカンマとともに使い、前文と逆の状況を示す。

noteKo.exampleTr: 저금리 대출은 소비를 늘리고, 반대로 고금리는 소비를 줄인다.
noteKo.usage: 보통 문장 앞에 쉼표와 함께 써서 반대 상황을 제시.

covered.ex: The course covered all the main topics.

de.en: part of a family name (De Blasio)

decade.ex: Prices have doubled in a decade.

declined.en: went down in amount or value
declined.ex: Sales declined sharply in the winter.

department.en: a part of a government or organisation
department.ex: He works in the health department.

departmental.ex: A departmental meeting is held every week.

difficult.ex: The test was difficult for everyone.

distribution.en: how something is shared across a group
distribution.ex: The distribution of income is very unequal.

do.en: used instead of repeating a verb
do.ex: I like tea, and my sister does too.

dominates.en: is the biggest or most important part

down.ex: He sat down on the bench.

dwindled.ex: The crowd dwindled as the rain began.

example.en: Our savings dwindled to almost nothing.
example.zh: 我們的存款逐漸減少到幾乎沒有。

note.usage: 不及物動詞，常見 dwindle to / from…to…；表示數量慢慢縮小。

noteEn.meaning: Became gradually smaller in number or size.
noteEn.usage: No object; often 'dwindle to' or 'from ... to ...'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Nuestros ahorros se redujeron casi a nada.

noteHi.exampleTr: हमारी बचत घटते-घटते लगभग खत्म हो गई।

noteJa.exampleTr: 私たちの貯金はほとんどゼロにまで減った。
noteJa.meaning: 次第に減った、先細りになった。
noteJa.usage: 自動詞。dwindle to ／ from … to … の形。

economic.ex: The country faces serious economic problems.

economists.en: experts who study money and trade

encompassing.ex: The plan, encompassing health and schools, was approved.

example.en: The course, encompassing art and history, is popular.
example.zh: 這門涵蓋藝術與歷史的課程很受歡迎。

note.usage: encompass 為及物動詞，正式；分詞常置名詞後作修飾：a tax encompassing all assets。

noteEn.usage: A formal verb; the -ing form often follows a noun: 'a tax encompassing all assets'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El curso, que abarca arte e historia, es muy popular.
noteEs.meaning: Que incluye o abarca muchas cosas.
noteEs.usage: Verbo formal transitivo; el participio suele ir tras el sustantivo.

noteHi.exampleTr: कला और इतिहास को शामिल करने वाला यह पाठ्यक्रम लोकप्रिय है।
noteHi.meaning: कई चीज़ों को शामिल करते हुए।
noteHi.usage: encompass औपचारिक सकर्मक क्रिया; संज्ञा के बाद कृदंत: a tax encompassing all assets।

noteJa.exampleTr: 美術と歴史を含むその講座は人気がある。
noteJa.usage: encompass は改まった他動詞。分詞で名詞を後ろから修飾することが多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 미술과 역사를 아우르는 그 강좌는 인기가 있다.
noteKo.usage: encompass는 격식 있는 타동사; 분사로 명사 뒤에서 수식.

end.en: the last part of a time
end.ex: We will meet again at the end of the month.

esri.en: Economic and Social Research Institute in Ireland
esri.ja: ESRI（アイルランド経済社会研究所）
esri.zh: ESRI（愛爾蘭經濟與社會研究所）

evaluated.en: judged how good or useful something is
evaluated.ex: The teacher evaluated each student's work.

even.ex: It is even colder today than yesterday.

ever.ex: The city is growing ever larger.

exemptions.en: permission not to pay or follow a rule
exemptions.ex: Students get exemptions from some fees.

example.en: Charities receive exemptions from some taxes.
example.zh: 慈善機構可豁免部分稅款。

note.meaning: 豁免；免除繳稅或遵守規定的特准。
note.usage: 常見 exemption from + 義務；tax exemptions；grant an exemption。

noteEn.meaning: Permission not to pay a tax or follow a rule.
noteEn.usage: Say 'exemption from something'; common in 'tax exemptions'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las organizaciones benéficas reciben exenciones de algunos impuestos.
noteEs.meaning: Permiso para no pagar un impuesto o no cumplir una norma.

noteHi.exampleTr: धर्मार्थ संस्थाओं को कुछ करों से छूट मिलती है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी कर या नियम से मुक्ति।
noteHi.usage: exemption from + कर्तव्य; tax exemptions; grant an exemption।

noteJa.exampleTr: 慈善団体は一部の税を免除されている。
noteJa.meaning: 税や規則の適用を免除されること。
noteJa.usage: exemption from ～、tax exemptions、grant an exemption の形。

noteKo.usage: exemption from ~, tax exemptions, grant an exemption.

family.ex: She lives with her family in Cork.

farm.ex: They run a dairy farm in Kerry.

farms.ex: They run a dairy farm in Kerry.

finance.ex: She works in finance at a big bank.

findings.ex: The findings will be shared next month.

firms.ex: Tech firms are hiring more engineers.

found.ex: The study found that sleep improves memory.

fraught.ex: The talks were fraught with difficulty.

funded.ex: The project is funded by the city.

further.ex: Wages are lower further down the company.

gives.ex: The plan gives more money to schools.

growing.ex: There is growing interest in electric cars.

had.ex: In 1990 the town had two cinemas.

half.ex: Half of the class was absent today.

has.en: owns or holds; also forms perfect tense

have.ja: 持つ；〜しなければならない

held.ex: The share held by women has grown.

high.ex: Prices are very high this year.

higher.ex: Prices are higher in the city.

hold.ex: They hold shares in the company.

holds.ex: The bank holds most of the debt.

home.ex: Many students rent a room in a family home.

homes.ex: Many students rent a room in a family home.

household.en: belonging to the people in a home

households.en: people living together in one home

houses.ex: They bought a house near the sea.

however.ex: It was cold. However, we went out.

ideas.ex: Send us your ideas for the party.

illiquid.en: not easy to sell or turn into cash

example.en: Property is illiquid, so it can take months to sell.
example.zh: 房地產難以變現，可能要幾個月才能賣出。

note.meaning: 形容資產難以迅速出售或換成現金。
note.usage: 常用於財經語境，修飾 assets / investments；反義詞為 liquid。

noteEn.meaning: Not easy to sell quickly or change into cash.
noteEn.usage: Used in finance, often with 'assets'; the opposite is 'liquid'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La vivienda es ilíquida, así que venderla puede llevar meses.
noteEs.meaning: Que no se puede vender o convertir en dinero rápidamente.
noteEs.usage: Se usa en finanzas con 'assets'; el contrario es 'liquid'.

noteHi.exampleTr: संपत्ति अतरल होती है, इसलिए बेचने में महीनों लग सकते हैं।
noteHi.meaning: ऐसी संपत्ति जिसे जल्दी नकद में बदलना कठिन हो।
noteHi.usage: वित्तीय संदर्भ में assets के साथ प्रयोग; उल्टा शब्द liquid।

noteJa.exampleTr: 不動産は換金しにくいので、売るのに数か月かかることもある。
noteJa.meaning: すぐに売ったり現金化したりしにくいこと。
noteJa.usage: 金融の文脈で assets などを修飾する。反対語は liquid。

noteKo.exampleTr: 부동산은 현금화가 어려워 파는 데 몇 달이 걸릴 수 있다.
noteKo.meaning: 빨리 팔거나 현금으로 바꾸기 어려운 상태.
noteKo.usage: 금융 문맥에서 assets 등을 수식; 반대말은 liquid.

in.en: inside; at a time or place

increased.ex: The number of visitors has increased.

indicate.ex: The results indicate a clear trend.

institute.en: an organisation for research or study
institute.ex: He works at a science institute.

jointly.ex: The house is jointly owned by the couple.

just.ex: I just want a glass of water.

left.ex: Two players were left out of the team.

less.ex: This road is less busy at night.

level.en: an amount or height on a scale
level.ex: The level of debt is too high.

levy.en: a tax that must be paid
levy.ex: The government added a levy on sugary drinks.

example.en: The council introduced a levy on plastic bags.
example.zh: 議會對塑膠袋開徵一項稅費。

note.meaning: 名詞指政府徵收的稅或費；動詞指徵收（稅款）。
note.usage: 常見 a levy on + 課稅對象；動詞 levy a tax on sth.。

noteEn.meaning: A tax or charge set by a government; as a verb, to charge a tax.
noteEn.usage: Say 'a levy on something'; verb: 'levy a tax on something'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El ayuntamiento introdujo un gravamen sobre las bolsas de plástico.
noteEs.meaning: Impuesto o cargo oficial; como verbo, imponer un impuesto.
noteEs.usage: Se dice 'a levy on' algo; verbo: 'levy a tax on'.

noteHi.exampleTr: परिषद ने प्लास्टिक थैलों पर शुल्क लगाया।
noteHi.meaning: सरकार द्वारा लगाया गया कर या शुल्क; क्रिया के रूप में कर लगाना।
noteHi.usage: a levy on + वस्तु; क्रिया: levy a tax on something।

noteJa.exampleTr: 議会はレジ袋に課徴金を導入した。
noteJa.meaning: 政府が課す税や負担金。動詞では「（税を）課す」。
noteJa.usage: a levy on + 対象。動詞は levy a tax on ～。

noteKo.usage: a levy on + 대상; 동사는 levy a tax on ~.

levying.ex: The city is levying a tax on hotels.

example.en: Several countries are levying taxes on carbon emissions.
example.zh: 好幾個國家正對碳排放課稅。

note.meaning: levy 的現在分詞，意為「徵收（稅款）」。
note.usage: 搭配 levy a tax / duty on sth.，比 charge 正式。

noteEn.meaning: The -ing form of 'levy': charging a tax.
noteEn.usage: Use 'levy a tax/duty on something'; more formal than 'charge'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Varios países están gravando las emisiones de carbono.
noteEs.meaning: Forma -ing de 'levy': imponer o cobrar un impuesto.
noteEs.usage: Se usa 'levy a tax/duty on'; más formal que 'charge'.

noteHi.exampleTr: कई देश कार्बन उत्सर्जन पर कर लगा रहे हैं।
noteHi.usage: levy a tax/duty on something; charge से अधिक औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: いくつかの国が炭素排出に課税している。
noteJa.meaning: levy の -ing 形で「（税を）課す」。
noteJa.usage: levy a tax / duty on ～ の形。charge より改まった語。

noteKo.exampleTr: 여러 나라가 탄소 배출에 세금을 부과하고 있다.
noteKo.usage: levy a tax/duty on ~ 형태; charge보다 격식 있음.

liable.ex: Anyone earning money is liable for tax.

example.en: Owners are liable for any damage their dogs cause.
example.zh: 狗主人須為狗造成的任何損害負責。

note.meaning: 有（法律）責任的；須繳納的。
note.usage: 常見 liable for + 費用／責任、liable to tax；另有 be liable to do（容易…）。

noteEn.usage: Use 'liable for' a cost or 'liable to tax'; 'liable to do' means likely to.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los dueños son responsables de los daños que causen sus perros.
noteEs.meaning: Obligado por ley a pagar o responder de algo.
noteEs.usage: 'liable for' + coste; 'liable to tax'; 'be liable to do' = tender a.

noteHi.exampleTr: कुत्ते के मालिक उसके किए नुकसान के लिए ज़िम्मेदार हैं।
noteHi.meaning: कानूनी रूप से ज़िम्मेदार; कर देने के लिए बाध्य।
noteHi.usage: liable for + खर्च/ज़िम्मेदारी, liable to tax; be liable to do = संभावना होना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 飼い主は犬が起こした損害に責任を負う。
noteJa.meaning: 法的責任がある、（税を）払う義務がある。
noteJa.usage: liable for ～、liable to tax。be liable to do は「～しがち」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 개 주인은 개가 끼친 피해에 책임을 진다.
noteKo.meaning: 법적 책임이 있는, (세금을) 낼 의무가 있는.
noteKo.usage: liable for ~, liable to tax; be liable to do는 '~하기 쉽다'.

looked.ex: The team looked at three plans.

looks.ex: This book looks at life in old Dublin.

loom.ex: Money worries loom large for students.
loom.ja: ますます大きな存在となる

lot.ex: I learned a lot from this course.

main.ex: The main problem is the cost.

make.ex: Women make up half of the team.

maximised.ex: Profits are maximised by cutting waste.

example.en: Sales were maximised by opening on weekends.
example.zh: 週末營業使銷售額達到最大。

note.usage: 英式拼法（美式 maximized）；常見 maximise profits / revenue。

noteEs.exampleTr: Las ventas se maximizaron abriendo los fines de semana.
noteEs.meaning: Llevado al nivel más alto posible.

noteHi.exampleTr: सप्ताहांत पर खुलने से बिक्री अधिकतम हुई।
noteHi.meaning: जितना हो सके उतना बड़ा किया गया।

noteJa.exampleTr: 週末に営業することで売上が最大化された。
noteJa.meaning: できるだけ大きくされた（最大化された）。
noteJa.usage: 英式つづり（米式 maximized）。maximise profits / revenue。

might.ex: We might go to the beach.

money.en: what you use to buy things
money.ex: They saved money for a new car.

more.en: a larger amount; more than: over
more.ex: She has worked here for more than ten years.

much.ex: This bag is much heavier than mine.

necessitate.ex: The changes will necessitate new training.

example.en: The new law will necessitate higher spending.
example.zh: 新法將使增加支出成為必要。

note.usage: 正式用語，主詞多為事物：X necessitates Y / doing sth.。

noteEn.usage: Formal; the subject is usually a thing: X necessitates Y.

noteEs.exampleTr: La nueva ley hará necesario un mayor gasto.
noteEs.usage: Formal; el sujeto suele ser una cosa: X necessitates Y.

noteHi.exampleTr: नया कानून अधिक खर्च को ज़रूरी बना देगा।
noteHi.meaning: किसी चीज़ को ज़रूरी बना देना।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक; कर्ता प्रायः कोई स्थिति: X necessitates Y।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新しい法律は支出の増加を必要とするだろう。
noteJa.meaning: ～を必要とさせる、不可欠にする。
noteJa.usage: 改まった語。主語は物事が多い：X necessitates Y。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 법은 지출 증가를 필요로 할 것이다.
noteKo.usage: 격식체; 주어는 주로 사물: X necessitates Y.

net.en: left after debts or costs are taken away
net.ex: His net income is lower than he thought.

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went for a walk.

new.ex: They opened a new shop in town.

notably.ex: Notably, sales rose during the winter.

notoriously.en: in a way well known for being bad
notoriously.hi: बदनाम रूप से; प्रसिद्ध रूप से

number.ex: A number of students were late today.

out.ex: She left out the hard questions.

own.en: to have something as your property

pay.ex: I will pay for the tickets.

pensions.en: money saved or paid after you stop working
pensions.ex: Many workers worry about their pensions.

people.ex: Many people came to the festival.

per.ex: The ticket costs ten euro per person.

permit.ex: The rules permit two bags per person.

pitched.ex: The price was pitched too high.

politically.en: in a way connected with politics

poorest.ex: The poorest families need the most help.

principal.ex: Tourism is the principal industry here.

problems.en: things that are difficult or wrong
problems.ex: We talked about our problems at school.

proportion.ex: A large proportion of students live nearby.

raise.ex: The school wants to raise money for books.

raised.ex: The charity raised ten thousand dollars.

paragraphs: A new study looks at how Ireland could tax wealth. Wealth means the things people own, like houses, farms, businesses and savings.
The ESRI and the Department of Finance wrote the study. They say Irish families are much richer than ten years ago. But the richest 10% of homes own almost half of all the wealth.

The study gives two choices. A tax could cover almost everything people own. Then only the richest 1.5% of homes would pay. Or the tax could leave out family homes, farms and businesses. Then many more people would pay.
There are problems too. It is hard to know the value of a farm or a business. Some people own a lot but have little cash.
In 1990, twelve European countries had a wealth tax. Now only three have one: Norway, Spain and Switzerland.

A new study has looked at different ways Ireland could tax wealth. The Department of Finance paid for the study, which was written by economists from the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI) and the department.

The study found that the total wealth of Irish households in 2023 was two and a half times higher than ten years before. The poorer half of households now has a bigger share than before, but the richest 10% still own almost half of all wealth.

The authors compared two main ideas. If the tax covered almost everything people own, except pensions, it could start at a very high level and only affect the richest 1.5% of households. But if family homes, farms and businesses were left out, the tax would have to start much lower, and many more households would pay it. The study says what is taxed matters more for the money raised than where the tax starts.
Taxing homes, farms and businesses would be politically difficult. These things are hard to value and hard to sell quickly, so even rich families might not have the cash to pay.
In 1990, twelve European countries had a yearly wealth tax. Today only Norway, Spain and Switzerland do.

A study funded by the Department of Finance has examined several options for taxing wealth in Ireland. It was written by Rachel Slaymaker and Chi Tran of the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI) and Federica De Blasio and Emmet Ryan, economists at the department.

The authors found that total net household wealth in 2023 was two and a half times its level a decade earlier. Although the poorest half of households now hold a larger share, the wealthiest 10 per cent still control almost half of all wealth. Business assets make up a growing proportion at the top, while the family home is the main asset further down.

To raise the most revenue, a tax would apply to all assets except pensions, with no exemptions for homes, farms or businesses. The threshold could then be set so high that only the richest 1.5 per cent of households would pay. Generous exemptions, by contrast, would require a much lower threshold. The report concludes that the breadth of the tax base matters more than the threshold.

However, taxing such assets would be politically sensitive, and they are difficult to value and sell. In 1990, twelve European countries had an annual wealth tax; today only Norway, Spain and Switzerland do.

A study commissioned by the Department of Finance has weighed up a range of approaches to taxing wealth. Its authors are Rachel Slaymaker and Chi Tran of the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI), alongside departmental economists Federica De Blasio and Emmet Ryan.

Their analysis shows that net household wealth in 2023 had swelled to two and a half times its level a decade earlier. Although the less affluent half of households now commands a larger slice, the wealthiest tenth still holds close to half of the total. Business assets loom ever larger at the top of the distribution, whereas the family home dominates further down.

A levy on all assets bar pensions, with no carve-outs for homes, farms or firms, would yield the most revenue and could be pitched so high that only the richest 1.5 per cent of households were caught. Lavish exemptions, conversely, would force the threshold sharply lower. The breadth of the base, the authors argue, trumps the level of the threshold.

Yet such a broad levy would be politically fraught, and these assets are illiquid and notoriously hard to value. Tellingly, the number of European countries with an annual net wealth tax has dwindled from twelve in 1990 to just three today: Norway, Spain and Switzerland.

A study funded by the Department of Finance has evaluated a number of alternative approaches to the taxation of wealth. The research was conducted jointly by Rachel Slaymaker and Chi Tran of the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI) and Federica De Blasio and Emmet Ryan of the department.

The findings indicate that aggregate net household wealth in 2023 was approximately two and a half times its level ten years previously. While the share held by the less affluent half of households has increased, the wealthiest 10 per cent continue to account for almost half of total wealth. Business assets constitute a growing proportion at the upper end of the distribution, whereas the family home represents the principal asset for other households.

Revenue would be maximised by a broadly based tax encompassing all assets other than pensions, which would permit a threshold so high that merely 1.5 per cent of households would be liable. Conversely, extensive exemptions would necessitate a substantially lower threshold. The authors consequently conclude that the breadth of the tax base is more significant than the threshold itself.

Nevertheless, taxing such assets would be politically contentious, given that they are illiquid and difficult to value. Notably, the number of European countries levying an annual net wealth tax has declined from twelve in 1990 to only three: Norway, Spain and Switzerland.
